answer: An answer must cite at least 3 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. Because the delta index resolves every citation against the nebula checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the copper audit keeps the resolved set. Copying the same citations across 103 aliases as a result pays the authoring cost 103 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
